title: Tanzanian Dagaa Stew
community: Lake Victoria regions — the affordable everyday protein stew
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Dagaa — dried dagaa (lake sardines) cooked in a spiced tomato-onion sauce. The most affordable, nutritious protein stew of Lake Victoria — eaten with ugali by millions of Tanzanians daily.
longDesc: Dagaa stew is the everyday protein of Tanzania's lake regions — dried lake sardines in a simple tomato sauce, reconstituted into a nutritious stew. The meal most Tanzanian families around Lake Victoria eat every day.
ingredients: 200g dried dagaa — rinsed and picked over
steps: Rinse dagaa thoroughly in cold water. Pick out any debris.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices.
Simmer covered 12—15 minutes until dagaa are soft and well flavoured.
chefTips: Rinse dagaa thoroughly — can be sandy.
Do not over-stir — dagaa break apart.
Stew should be thick, not watery.
cookingScience: Dried dagaa absorb water during simmering — reconstituting to twice their dried volume. Rehydration also softens bones which become edible after simmering, providing significant calcium.
sustainabilityTips: Dagaa are one of the most sustainable protein sources on earth — abundant, fast-reproducing.
healthBenefits: One of Africa's most nutritionally complete affordable foods.
culturalNote: Dagaa stew is the food security of Lake Victoria's communities — the affordable protein that ensures families are nourished even in difficult times.
